newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland police probe killing of Catholic girl.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland police probe killing of Catholic girl.

text.p: A young Catholic girl was shot and fatally wounded in Northern Ireland early on Tuesday and police said they were questioning a man about the attack, but were unsure whether it was sectarian.

The girl was sleeping at a house in the staunchly Protestant village of Aghalee some 30 miles (50 km) southwest of Belfast in the early hours of Tuesday when a gunman entered the house and shot her from close range, hitting her in the head and face.

The girl, who was believed to be 18 years old, was taken to hospital in Belfast where security sources said she died several hours after the shooting. Residents of the village said the girl had been staying with her Protestant boyfriend.
The arrest was made after police searched a house close to the one where the girl had been staying. No further details were available.
The shooting occurred at a period of high tension between Protestants and Catholics after days of Catholic rioting last week over Orange Order parades.
